finding.claim: The /mirror endpoint host check uses a bare string suffix (endswith('example.com')) with no dot boundary or exact match, so attacker-owned domains such as evilexample.com pass. The unvalidated URL is then fetched server-side with httpx, enabling SSRF to internal or metadata addresses via DNS rebinding.

trace.note: url: str taken directly from the query string
host.endswith('example.com') is the only guard; no dot boundary, no exact match
Original unparsed url passed to c.get(), so the request goes to whatever the name resolves to
Returns only len(r.text), limiting the attacker to a size oracle

finding.guards_checked: Host suffix check at mirror.py:13 is the only guard; it is a bare suffix match that admits evilexample.com and similar. ALLOWED_SUFFIX='.example.com' (mirror.py:7) is defined but unused. No scheme allowlist. No resolved-IP or private/loopback/link-local/metadata block, and no IP pinning, so DNS rebinding works. Redirects are not followed (httpx default), which removes the redirect-to-internal path. Route has no auth dependency. The /ping route (mirror.py:20-24) uses a hardcoded URL and was not reported. A parser differential between urlparse and httpx was considered but not confirmed.

verdict.guard_found: none. The only check is `host.endswith("example.com")` at mirror.py:13, a bare suffix match with no dot boundary or exact match, so it admits evilexample.com. ALLOWED_SUFFIX at mirror.py:7 is defined but never used. There is no scheme allowlist, no resolved-IP or private-address block, and no auth dependency on the route. httpx defaults to follow_redirects=False at mirror.py:15, which only removes the redirect path.
verdict.reason: The `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16 after only the bare suffix check at mirror.py:13, so an attacker can use a domain they control, such as evilexample.com, to point at an internal or metadata address. The claim's "via DNS rebinding" is an unnecessary detail, since plain DNS control of the attacker's domain is enough, but the core SSRF finding holds and the response leaks only len(r.text) at mirror.py:17.
